also: use a word in a sentence

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, deponent; with the ablative
terms.comment: The thing used is in the ablative: oculīs ūtī, cōnsiliō ūtī. Ūtī also means “enjoy, have the benefit of” and “treat (someone)”.

evidence: Cic. Sen. 36: tantum cibī et pōtiōnis adhibendum
terms.comment: To bring something in for a purpose: care, force, a doctor.

phrases.english: (— Is that Epidicus I see? —) You certainly have the use of your eyes.

phrases.latin: dē rēbus ipsīs ūtere tuō jūdiciō
phrases.english: on the matter itself, use your own judgement
to make the best use of
